about: The bench's fixed world, shaped like one the New Story wizard builds. Invented, with no adult text. A journey through danger: it opens a day out on the road, half a day short of the first well, so the road's set pieces (the dust-riders, the sabotage at the well, the sandstorm and the Glass Flats) come within a run, and the riders come to the PC whatever they pick. It is made to bring about everything the Narrator does: Checks on risky Choices, Plot Threads that move on and resolve (the first within a day of story time), secrets for NPCs to learn, Loose Ends, lore to grow, a deadly crossing, and people who may die. actions holds the fixed words of the Rewrite, Edit and World Change the bench sends.

save.title: The Salt Road
save.artStyle: Cinematic Photorealism: Ultra-detailed photorealistic style capturing hyper-accurate physics, micro-surface textures, natural volumetric light dispersion, realistic lens depth of field, and true-to-life subsurface scattering, indistinguishable from high-resolution digital cinema footage.
save.worldBrief: A desert frontier where salt is carted by camel caravan from the coast to the inland city of Kesh, and water is worth more than coin. The Governor's water tax is choking the well-keepers, and the road between is long, hot and lawless.
save.startingHook: Wren joined Tamsin's salt caravan at Port Lell to carry a satchel of sealed letters inland to Governor Hale at Kesh. At the border post, Captain Vane of the Border Guard searched the wagons, took Wren's pistol and chose to ride along. A day out, the caravan has halted in the shade of the Red Teeth to rest the camels before the last push to the Well of Ashar, and Jory has seen riders on the dunes behind them.

pc.name: Wren
pc.background: A courier for the Lell merchants' guild for ten years, paid well to carry what others won't. She owes the guild for a lost cargo and needs this delivery to clear the debt.
pc.physicalTraits: Lean, sun-browned woman in her thirties, short black hair, a pale scar through her left eyebrow, grey eyes.
pc.skills: Riding, reading people, a quick knife, finding water by the plants around it, keeping her mouth shut.
pc.personality: Wary and dry-humoured, slow to trust and quick to notice. Keeps her word once she gives it.

importantCharacters.name: Tamsin
importantCharacters.description: Stocky woman in her sixties, white hair in a single long braid, deeply weathered face, missing the two smallest fingers of her right hand, indigo head-wrap, long leather vest over a faded red robe. The caravan's owner and master, gruff and shrewd.

importantCharacters.name: Jory
importantCharacters.description: Gangly boy of about fourteen, red curly hair, freckles, a too-large green tunic belted with rope, barefoot. Tamsin's camel boy, eager to please.

importantCharacters.name: Captain Vane
importantCharacters.description: Tall man in his forties, shaved head, close-trimmed black beard, a burn scar down the left side of his neck, dusty blue officer's coat with brass buttons, a sabre at his hip. A Border Guard officer, cold and watchful.

worldRules: Water is wealth: a day on the Glass Flats without water can kill, and every caravan counts its skins.
There is no magic; the desert's dangers are heat, storms, thirst and people.
Pistols are rare and licensed by the Border Guard; most people carry blades.
Breaking a Governor's seal is a hanging crime.
plotThreads: Ossery, the well-keeper at the Well of Ashar, slits caravans' waterskins in the night so they must buy his water at ruinous prices, and Jory cut the first one for him for a coin. Captain Vane is hunting this saboteur, suspects Tamsin, and means to arrest her at the Well tomorrow unless someone shows him the truth.

The sealed letter to Governor Hale names his own steward, Marrick, as the man selling salt-tax receipts to the Free Wells; Marrick's dust-riders under Sefa have trailed the caravan from the border and will strike at dusk tonight, at the Red Teeth or on the road beyond, to take Wren's satchel.

The Free Wells, a league of well-keepers crushed by the water tax, will seize the Well of Ashar in three days and close the salt road; Tamsin secretly carries their demand to the Governor, hidden in her saddle, and would sooner die than let it be found.

worldBible.title: The salt road and the water tax
worldBible.content: Salt is carted from the pans at Port Lell to the city of Kesh, twelve days by camel. Governor Hale taxes every skin of water drawn on the road, and the well-keepers who pay it are going hungry. Caravans resent the tax; the Border Guard enforces it.

worldBible.title: Tamsin
worldBible.content: A stocky woman in her sixties, white hair in a single long braid, a deeply weathered face, missing the two smallest fingers of her right hand, in an indigo head-wrap and a long leather vest over a faded red robe. Owner of the caravan, thirty years on the road. She lost two fingers to a rope on a camel's girth. Her son Pell drowned in the spring flood two years ago, and she has not laughed since. Governor Hale owes her a large debt for salt he never paid for. Secretly she sympathises with the Free Wells and carries their demand to the Governor, sewn into her saddle. She trusts Jory like a grandson.

worldBible.title: Jory
worldBible.content: A gangly boy of about fourteen with red curly hair and freckles, in a too-large green tunic belted with rope, barefoot. An orphan from Port Lell who cannot read. At the Well of Ashar last season, Ossery paid him a silver coin to cut one waterskin, telling him it was a joke on a rival; he did, and has been sick with guilt since, sure that Tamsin would turn him out if she knew. He would confess to someone who was kind to him.

worldBible.title: Captain Vane
worldBible.content: A tall man in his forties with a shaved head, a close-trimmed black beard and a burn scar down the left side of his neck, in a dusty blue officer's coat with brass buttons, a sabre at his hip. A Border Guard captain sent by the Governor to find who is sabotaging caravans. His burn scar is from a well fire he pulled two children out of. Honest, ruthless and proud; he will use his sabre if crossed, and he will hang whoever he decides is guilty. He suspects Tamsin because her caravans are never hit. He keeps Wren's pistol in his saddlebag.

worldBible.title: Ossery
worldBible.content: Keeper of the Well of Ashar: a thin, smiling man in his fifties with a long grey moustache, wearing an old Border Guard coat with brass buttons he bought from a deserter. He slits caravans' waterskins at night, then sells them water at ten times its worth. He fears Vane, and would kill to keep his secret. One brass button is missing from his coat.

worldBible.title: Marrick
worldBible.content: Governor Hale's steward, soft-spoken and patient. He sells forged salt-tax receipts to the Free Wells and has grown rich on it. He has paid a band of dust-riders to take every letter bound for the Governor this season.

worldBible.title: The dust-riders
worldBible.content: Five hired riders on fast horses, faces wrapped in grey cloth, led by a woman called Sefa with a crossbow. They strike at dusk from the dunes, want only the letters, and kill anyone who fights back.

worldBible.title: The Free Wells
worldBible.content: A league of desert well-keepers sworn to end the water tax. They mean to seize the Well of Ashar at the new moon, three nights off, and close the salt road until the Governor gives way. Ossery is not one of them; they despise him.

worldBible.title: The Well of Ashar
worldBible.content: The last good well before the Glass Flats: a stone ring under three palms, a keeper's hut of mud brick, and a walled yard for camels. Every caravan must water here.

worldBible.title: The Glass Flats
worldBible.content: Two days of white salt crust between Ashar and Kesh, flat as a table and blinding at noon. Mirages lead travellers astray, the crust breaks over sinkholes of brine, and a caravan that runs out of water there dies.

worldBible.title: The Red Teeth
worldBible.content: A ridge of red sandstone spires a day out from the border post and half a day short of the Well of Ashar, the only shelter from sandstorms on the road, and a favourite ambush ground.

worldBible.title: Governor Hale and Kesh
worldBible.content: Kesh is a walled city of white domes on the far side of the Glass Flats. Governor Hale is vain and short of money, and trusts Marrick completely.

actions.rewrite: Slow down, and let the people present react to what just happened before anything new happens.
actions.edit: Far to the east, a thin brown haze stood along the horizon.
actions.worldChange: A great sandstorm is building in the east and will reach the salt road within two days.
